math.scope: Actual item frames, zero and nonzero classes, numeric/string/mixed IDs, renamed isomorphs and one-sided empty graphs; minimal view API is not a native UI substitute.

rawFullRows.name: Time- and space-constructible functions
rawFullRows.pic: A machine computes the bound t(n) in binary within t(n) steps for n², n log n and 2ⁿ, while a step counter shows the clock never overruns the budget it measures.

rawFullRows.name: Time hierarchy theorem
rawFullRows.pic: A clocked universal machine simulates each machine on its own description and does the opposite; the machine-versus-input table shows the flipped diagonal escaping every machine faster than the clock.

rawFullRows.name: Space hierarchy theorem
rawFullRows.pic: The diagonalizing machine marks off s(n) cells and simulates within them, halting any simulation that loops; a meter shows it never crosses its marked fence.

rawFullRows.name: P ≠ EXPTIME and L ≠ PSPACE
rawFullRows.pic: A ladder of classes TIME(n), TIME(n²), …, TIME(2ⁿ) with a separating language at each rung; clicking a rung shows the diagonal language that lives there and not below.

rawFullRows.name: Nondeterministic time hierarchy theorem
rawFullRows.pic: Lazy diagonalization: on a long interval of input lengths the diagonalizer waits, then flips the answer once, and the intervals and the single disagreement point are drawn on a number line.

rawFullRows.name: Linear speedup theorem
rawFullRows.pic: Pack k tape symbols into one super-symbol; the compressed machine’s step count is plotted against the original’s and falls by about a factor of k, which is why constants are ignored.

rawFullRows.name: Hopcroft–Paul–Valiant: time t fits in space t/log t
rawFullRows.pic: Play the pebble game on a computation graph the reader draws: pebbles may be placed when all predecessors hold one, and the strategy found uses far fewer pebbles than nodes.

rawFullRows.name: Ladner’s theorem
rawFullRows.pic: SAT is “blown full of holes” by padding on stretches of input lengths chosen by a slow diagonalizer; the stretches where it is hard or trivial are shown alternating on a log scale.

rawFullRows.name: Candidates for NP-intermediate: factoring and graph isomorphism
rawFullRows.pic: Colour refinement on two graphs the reader draws: vertex colours split round by round, and graphs with different colour counts are certified non-isomorphic, while regular graphs defeat it.

rawFullRows.name: Oracle machines and relativized classes
rawFullRows.pic: A polynomial-time machine consults an oracle box in one step; switching the oracle between a SAT solver and a random set changes which problems the same machine can decide.

rawFullRows.name: Baker–Gill–Solovay: relativization barrier
rawFullRows.pic: With a PSPACE-complete oracle, P and NP coincide; with an oracle built stage by stage against each machine, they differ — both constructions are stepped through side by side.

rawFullRows.name: A provably intractable natural problem
rawFullRows.pic: Equivalence of regular expressions with an exponentiation operator is EXPSPACE-complete, so outside PSPACE; the expression size explodes when the reader expands the exponents.

rawFullRows.name: On the Computational Complexity of Algorithms

paper.authors: J. Hartmanis and R. E. Stearns
paper.title: On the Computational Complexity of Algorithms
paper.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 117: 285–306

rawFullRows.pic: Race multitape machines under a time bound T and a sufficiently larger one: a diagonal machine simulates each fast machine on its own description and does the opposite, while a second panel shows linear speed-up by packing several tape symbols into one.

rawFullRows.name: 3-dimensional matching is NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Variable gadgets are rings of triples that must be taken all-even or all-odd; clause triples plug in, and a satisfying assignment the reader picks yields a perfect matching.

rawFullRows.name: Exact cover and tiling puzzles are NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Pentomino tiling as exact cover: rows of the incidence matrix are placements, and a backtracking search (dancing links) finds tilings while its node count grows rapidly with board size.

rawFullRows.name: PARTITION and KNAPSACK are NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: A subset-sum instance is turned into a partition instance by adding two balancing numbers; the reader splits the numbers into two piles and the balance scale tips or levels.

rawFullRows.name: Weak versus strong NP-hardness
rawFullRows.pic: Knapsack’s dynamic program runs fast when numbers are small and blows up with digit count, while 3-PARTITION stays hard even with numbers written in unary — both timed live.

rawFullRows.name: Integer linear programming is NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Each clause becomes a linear inequality over 0/1 variables; the LP relaxation’s fractional optimum is drawn next to the integer points, which may all be infeasible.

rawFullRows.name: MAX-CUT is NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Drag vertices between two sides to cut as many edges as possible; the gadget from not-all-equal 3SAT makes large cuts correspond to satisfying assignments.

rawFullRows.name: SET-COVER and HITTING-SET are NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Vertex cover is set cover where each vertex covers its edges; the reader picks sets to cover a universe and the counter compares with the optimum found by search.

rawFullRows.name: Planar 3-colouring is NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Every edge crossing is replaced by a crossover gadget that forces opposite corners to share colours; the reader colours the gadget and checks it can never cheat.

rawFullRows.name: Hard puzzles: Sudoku, Minesweeper and friends
rawFullRows.pic: Minesweeper wires and gates are laid out on a board; whether a revealed position is consistent encodes a circuit’s satisfiability, checked as the reader edits the circuit.

rawFullRows.name: Schaefer’s dichotomy theorem
rawFullRows.pic: Pick the allowed constraint types of a Boolean CSP; the tool checks the six tractable cases — Horn, dual-Horn, 2-CNF, affine, 0- and 1-valid — and otherwise shows a reduction from 3SAT.

rawFullRows.name: Mahaney’s theorem: no sparse NP-complete sets unless P = NP
rawFullRows.pic: A reduction to a sparse set must map many formulas onto few strings; the self-reduction tree of SAT is pruned using these collisions until only polynomially many branches remain.

rawFullRows.name: Berman–Hartmanis isomorphism conjecture
rawFullRows.pic: Padding functions turn reductions between known NP-complete problems into polynomial-time bijections, shown as a perfect matching between instances of SAT and CLIQUE of bounded size.

rawFullRows.name: Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems

paper.title: Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems
paper.venue: in R. E. Miller and J. W. Thatcher (eds.), Complexity of Computer Computations, Plenum Press: 85–103

rawFullRows.pic: Karp’s tree of 21 problems drawn as a graph rooted at SAT: click an edge to watch a concrete small formula, graph or list of numbers transformed into the next problem, and a solution mapped back the other way.

rawFullRows.name: TAUTOLOGY is coNP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: A formula is a tautology exactly when its negation is unsatisfiable; the truth table of a typed formula is checked row by row, with a falsifying row as the only short certificate of “no”.

rawFullRows.name: Pratt certificates: PRIMES is in NP ∩ coNP
rawFullRows.pic: Type a prime p; the certificate — a generator of order p − 1 and the factorization of p − 1, each factor certified recursively — is drawn as a tree and verified node by node.

rawFullRows.name: Factoring lies in NP ∩ coNP
rawFullRows.pic: The complete prime factorization, with Pratt certificates for each factor, certifies both “N has a factor below k” and its negation, checked on a number the reader types.

rawFullRows.name: Σ₂ and Π₂: two quantifiers
rawFullRows.pic: MIN-FORMULA: is there a shorter equivalent formula? The ∃ guesses a small formula and the ∀ checks all assignments; both search layers are shown for a typed formula.

rawFullRows.name: The polynomial hierarchy
rawFullRows.pic: A tower of classes Σₖ and Πₖ with arrows for inclusions; dragging a quantifier prefix ∃∀∃… onto the tower places a problem at its level.

rawFullRows.name: If Σₖ = Πₖ the hierarchy collapses to level k
rawFullRows.pic: Merging two adjacent quantifiers of the same kind lets every higher level fold down; toggling the hypothesis animates the tower telescoping to level k.

rawFullRows.name: Σₖ-SAT is complete for level k
rawFullRows.pic: A quantified formula with k alternating blocks is evaluated as a game tree; the Cook–Levin tableau construction is shown carrying over block by block.

rawFullRows.name: Alternating Turing machines
rawFullRows.pic: A computation tree with ∃ and ∀ nodes is evaluated bottom-up — OR at existential nodes, AND at universal ones — and the reader flips leaf outcomes to change the verdict.

rawFullRows.name: Alternating polynomial time equals PSPACE
rawFullRows.pic: TQBF is solved by an alternating machine in linear time, and conversely an alternating computation tree is evaluated depth-first with a stack whose size is read out.

rawFullRows.name: Alternating logarithmic space equals P
rawFullRows.pic: Circuit evaluation as a game: the existential player claims a gate is true and the universal player challenges an input wire, walking down the circuit with only a gate pointer in memory.

rawFullRows.name: PH ⊆ PSPACE
rawFullRows.pic: Each level of the hierarchy is a bounded-quantifier TQBF instance; the space used to evaluate it recursively is plotted against k and stays polynomial.

rawFullRows.name: Time–space lower bounds for SAT
rawFullRows.pic: A fast, small-space SAT algorithm would let alternation speed up any computation (guess midpoints, check one), contradicting the hierarchy theorem; the trade-off curve of ruled-out (time, space) pairs is drawn.

rawFullRows.name: Boolean circuits and circuit size
rawFullRows.pic: Drag AND, OR and NOT gates onto a canvas and wire them; the circuit’s truth table, size and depth are computed live, and a ripple-carry adder is built as an example.

rawFullRows.name: Most functions need circuits of size about 2ⁿ/n (Shannon)
rawFullRows.pic: The number of circuits with s gates is plotted against the 2^(2ⁿ) Boolean functions on n inputs on a log–log scale; the curves cross near s = 2ⁿ/n.

rawFullRows.name: Every function has circuits of size O(2ⁿ/n) (Lupanov)
rawFullRows.pic: The truth table is cut into blocks and shared sub-functions are computed once; the circuit size for random functions is plotted against 2ⁿ/n and against the naive 2ⁿ·n.

rawFullRows.name: P/poly and advice
rawFullRows.pic: A machine receives an advice string depending only on the input length; the reader edits the advice for each length and sees which languages become decidable.

rawFullRows.name: P ⊆ P/poly
rawFullRows.pic: The tableau of a polynomial-time machine is unrolled into a grid of identical local gadgets; the circuit size is plotted against running time squared.

rawFullRows.name: P/poly contains undecidable languages
rawFullRows.pic: The unary halting language has at most one string per length, so a one-bit advice per length decides it; the advice bits are shown as a sequence no machine can compute.

rawFullRows.name: CIRCUIT-SAT is NP-complete
rawFullRows.pic: A verifier is compiled into a circuit with the certificate as free inputs; the reader searches for satisfying inputs and the circuit lights up when one is found.

rawFullRows.name: Karp–Lipton theorem
rawFullRows.pic: If small SAT circuits existed, a Π₂ statement could guess the circuit, test it by self-reduction and use it; the proof is animated as quantifiers swapping and the hierarchy folding.

rawFullRows.name: Meyer’s theorem: EXP ⊆ P/poly implies EXP = Σ₂
rawFullRows.pic: An exponential computation’s tableau is described by a small circuit that a Σ₂ machine guesses and checks locally, cell by cell, as the reader scrolls the tableau.

rawFullRows.name: NC and AC: shallow circuits
rawFullRows.pic: Circuits for the same function laid out by depth: a balanced XOR tree has logarithmic depth, while a chain has linear depth; the depth readout classifies each design.

rawFullRows.name: Parallel prefix: addition in logarithmic depth
rawFullRows.pic: Carry-lookahead computes all carries with a prefix network; the depth of the prefix tree grows like log n against the ripple-carry adder’s n, both drawn.

rawFullRows.name: Circuit value problem is P-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Any polynomial-time computation becomes a circuit by a log-space transducer; evaluating it layer by layer seems inherently sequential, and its depth is read out.

rawFullRows.name: NC¹ ⊆ L ⊆ NL ⊆ NC²
rawFullRows.pic: A logarithmic-depth formula is evaluated depth-first with a pointer stack; reachability is computed in depth log² n by repeated Boolean matrix squaring.

rawFullRows.name: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits

paper.title: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits
paper.venue: Transactions of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers 57 (12): 713–723

rawFullRows.pic: Wire relay contacts in series and parallel and see the network’s hindrance written as a Boolean expression; simplify it with Shannon’s rules and watch the circuit lose contacts while its truth table stays fixed, ending with his relay adder.

rawFullRows.name: Probabilistic Turing machines and BPP
rawFullRows.pic: Run a randomized algorithm many times on one input; the fraction of accepting runs is plotted and must stay above 2/3 on yes-inputs and below 1/3 on no-inputs.

rawFullRows.name: RP, coRP and ZPP
rawFullRows.pic: Three panels show one-sided error (never wrong on no-inputs), the opposite side, and zero error with a random running time whose histogram is drawn.

rawFullRows.name: ZPP = RP ∩ coRP
rawFullRows.pic: Alternate an RP and a coRP algorithm until one gives a certain answer; the number of rounds needed is geometrically distributed, as the simulated histogram shows.

rawFullRows.name: Error reduction by repetition
rawFullRows.pic: Take the majority of k independent runs; the error probability is plotted on a log scale against k and falls in a straight line, matching the Chernoff bound.

rawFullRows.name: Schwartz–Zippel lemma
rawFullRows.pic: A nonzero polynomial of degree d over a grid Sⁿ is evaluated everywhere; its zeros are coloured, and their fraction never exceeds d/|S|, whatever polynomial the reader types.

rawFullRows.name: Polynomial identity testing
rawFullRows.pic: Two arithmetic circuits are compared at random points; when they differ, a witness point is found within a few trials, while expanding them symbolically would explode.

rawFullRows.name: Perfect matchings via random Tutte matrices
rawFullRows.pic: Fill the Tutte matrix of a graph with random numbers and compute its determinant; it is nonzero with high probability exactly when a perfect matching exists, tested on graphs the reader draws.

rawFullRows.name: Freivalds’ check of matrix products
rawFullRows.pic: Claimed product C = AB is tested by multiplying both sides by a random 0/1 vector; plant an error in C and it is caught at least half the time, at quadratic rather than cubic cost.

rawFullRows.name: PRIMES is in P (Agrawal–Kayal–Saxena)
rawFullRows.pic: The identity (X + a)ⁿ ≡ Xⁿ + a modulo (X^r − 1, n) is checked for small a; composites fail some check while primes pass all, and the running time is plotted against bit length.

rawFullRows.name: Random-walk algorithm for 2SAT
rawFullRows.pic: Start from a random assignment and flip a random variable of a violated clause; the Hamming distance to a fixed solution performs a random walk that hits zero in about n² steps.

rawFullRows.name: Adleman: BPP ⊆ P/poly
rawFullRows.pic: After amplification, a grid of inputs against random strings has bad cells so sparse that some column is good for every input; the reader shades bad cells and finds that column.

rawFullRows.name: Sipser–Gács–Lautemann: BPP ⊆ Σ₂ ∩ Π₂
rawFullRows.pic: A large set of accepting random strings can be covered by a few XOR-shifts of itself, a small one cannot; the reader tries shifts and sees the cube covered or not.

rawFullRows.name: PRIMES is in P

paper.authors: Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal and Nitin Saxena
paper.title: PRIMES is in P

rawFullRows.pic: Enter n and run the AKS test: find a small r with large multiplicative order of n, then check (X + a)ⁿ ≡ Xⁿ + a modulo (X^r − 1, n) for each a, and watch a Carmichael number that fools Fermat’s test fail one of these congruences.

rawFullRows.name: Interactive proof systems and IP
rawFullRows.pic: A message diagram between prover and verifier steps through rounds; the reader plays a cheating prover and watches the verifier’s acceptance rate stay below the soundness bound.

rawFullRows.name: Interactive proof for graph non-isomorphism
rawFullRows.pic: The verifier secretly permutes one of two graphs and asks which it was; for isomorphic graphs the reader, as prover, can only guess, and the success rate settles at one half.

rawFullRows.name: Arthur–Merlin games: AM and MA
rawFullRows.pic: Arthur’s coins are shown face up to Merlin; message diagrams for MA (Merlin first) and AM (Arthur first) are compared on the same problem.

rawFullRows.name: Goldwasser–Sipser: public coins suffice
rawFullRows.pic: Set lower-bound protocol: a random hash function maps a large set onto a target and a small set rarely hits it; the reader resizes the set and watches the hit rate separate.

rawFullRows.name: Graph isomorphism is not NP-complete unless PH collapses
rawFullRows.pic: Graph non-isomorphism in AM would put coNP in AM if GI were NP-complete, and the chain of inclusions animates the polynomial hierarchy collapsing to level two.

rawFullRows.name: Arithmetization
rawFullRows.pic: Type a Boolean formula: AND becomes multiplication, NOT x becomes 1 − x, and the resulting polynomial agrees with the formula on every 0/1 input in the table.

rawFullRows.name: Sum-check protocol
rawFullRows.pic: The prover sends a univariate polynomial each round and the verifier checks it at a random point; a lying prover is caught with high probability, tallied over repeated runs.

rawFullRows.name: coNP ⊆ IP (Lund–Fortnow–Karloff–Nisan)
rawFullRows.pic: Counting satisfying assignments of a formula becomes a sum of its arithmetization over the cube; the sum-check rounds certify the count zero for an unsatisfiable formula.

rawFullRows.name: IP = PSPACE (Shamir)
rawFullRows.pic: Quantifiers become products and sums, and degree-reduction steps keep polynomials small; the degree of each round’s polynomial is plotted with and without linearization.

rawFullRows.name: MIP = NEXP (Babai–Fortnow–Lund)
rawFullRows.pic: Two provers are questioned in separate rooms; cross-checking their answers catches inconsistent strategies, as a match-rate meter shows for strategies the reader designs.

rawFullRows.name: Program checking (Blum–Kannan)
rawFullRows.pic: A buggy sorting or gcd routine is wrapped in a checker that tests its outputs on random self-related inputs; planted bugs are detected at the predicted rate.

rawFullRows.name: The class #P
rawFullRows.pic: For a typed formula, the number of satisfying assignments is counted by exhaustive search, and the count, not just its non-zeroness, is the output.

rawFullRows.name: #SAT is #P-complete
rawFullRows.pic: The Cook–Levin reduction is checked to be parsimonious: accepting paths of a machine and satisfying assignments of the formula are matched one to one.

rawFullRows.name: Valiant: the permanent is #P-complete
rawFullRows.pic: Cycle covers of a weighted graph are enumerated and summed; clause and variable gadgets make the permanent equal to a multiple of the number of satisfying assignments.

rawFullRows.name: Permanent versus determinant
rawFullRows.pic: The same matrix gives determinant and permanent; Gaussian elimination computes the determinant fast, while the permanent’s term count explodes as n! in the timing plot.

rawFullRows.name: FKT: counting perfect matchings of planar graphs
rawFullRows.pic: Orient a planar graph so every face has an odd number of clockwise edges; the Pfaffian of the signed matrix then counts perfect matchings, checked against brute force.

rawFullRows.name: Valiant–Vazirani isolation lemma
rawFullRows.pic: Random parity constraints are added to a formula with many solutions; the histogram of surviving solution counts shows exactly one survivor with probability bounded below.

rawFullRows.name: ⊕P (parity P)
rawFullRows.pic: Only the parity of the number of solutions matters; the reader adds and removes solutions and watches the ⊕SAT bit toggle.

rawFullRows.name: Toda’s theorem: PH ⊆ P^#P
rawFullRows.pic: Quantifiers are replaced one by one by randomized parity tests, then the randomness is folded into a single count; each stage of the transformation is shown on a small quantified formula.

rawFullRows.name: Approximate counting with an NP oracle (Stockmeyer)
rawFullRows.pic: Random hash functions into 2ᵏ buckets are tried for growing k; the largest k for which some bucket stays occupied estimates log₂ of the number of solutions.

rawFullRows.name: Approximating the permanent by Markov chain Monte Carlo
rawFullRows.pic: A Markov chain on matchings of a bipartite graph mixes; sampled ratios of matching counts multiply into an estimate of the permanent that converges as the reader runs more steps.

rawFullRows.name: Random self-reducibility of the permanent
rawFullRows.pic: The permanent of A is recovered from permanents of random matrices A + tR on a line, interpolated by a low-degree polynomial — so an algorithm right on most inputs is right on all.

rawFullRows.name: Method of conditional expectations
rawFullRows.pic: A random assignment satisfies 7/8 of 3-clauses on average; fixing variables one at a time while never lowering the conditional expectation, plotted per step, finds such an assignment deterministically.

rawFullRows.name: Pseudorandom generators for derandomization
rawFullRows.pic: Short seeds are stretched into long strings; a gallery of small distinguishing circuits tries to tell them from truly random strings, and the advantage of each is read out.

rawFullRows.name: Impagliazzo’s hard-core lemma
rawFullRows.pic: A mildly hard function hides a dense hard-core set on which small circuits do no better than coin flips; the set is grown by boosting and highlighted on the input cube.

rawFullRows.name: Yao’s XOR lemma
rawFullRows.pic: XOR k independent copies of a mildly hard function; the best predictor’s advantage is plotted against k and decays exponentially toward one half.

rawFullRows.name: Nisan–Wigderson generator
rawFullRows.pic: Output bits apply a hard function to overlapping subsets of the seed chosen from a combinatorial design; the design’s small pairwise overlaps are drawn as a set system.

rawFullRows.name: Hardness versus randomness (Impagliazzo–Wigderson)
rawFullRows.pic: A slider for the circuit lower bound assumed on exponential time maps to the derandomization obtained, ending at P = BPP for exponential lower bounds.

rawFullRows.name: Derandomizing identity testing implies lower bounds (Kabanets–Impagliazzo)
rawFullRows.pic: The two-way street is drawn as a loop between “PIT ∈ P” and “the permanent needs large arithmetic circuits or NEXP needs large Boolean circuits”, with each implication expandable.

rawFullRows.name: Expander graphs and spectral gap
rawFullRows.pic: For a regular graph the reader edits, the second eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix and the edge expansion of every small set are computed; random regular graphs land near the optimum.

rawFullRows.name: Expander mixing lemma
rawFullRows.pic: Select two vertex sets S and T by brushing; the number of edges between them is compared with the random-graph prediction d|S||T|/n, and the deviation stays within λ√(|S||T|).

rawFullRows.name: Random walks on expanders save random bits
rawFullRows.pic: Replace independent samples by a random walk on an expander; the fraction of steps inside a bad set concentrates almost as well, while the random bits used grow far more slowly.

rawFullRows.name: Zig-zag product
rawFullRows.pic: A large graph and a small one combine by a step in the small cloud, a jump, and another small step; the degree stays fixed while the computed spectral gap remains bounded away from zero.

rawFullRows.name: Reingold: undirected connectivity in log space
rawFullRows.pic: A graph is repeatedly powered and zig-zagged until each component becomes an expander of logarithmic diameter, which a log-space walk can then explore exhaustively.

rawFullRows.name: Randomness extractors and the leftover hash lemma
rawFullRows.pic: A biased, correlated source with known min-entropy is hashed by a random universal hash; the output’s distance from uniform is measured and shrinks as the output is shortened.

rawFullRows.name: Gap problems and hardness of approximation
rawFullRows.pic: A reduction maps yes-instances to fully satisfiable formulas and no-instances to formulas where at most a fraction ρ can be satisfied; the gap is drawn as a forbidden band on the value axis.

rawFullRows.name: Probabilistically checkable proofs
rawFullRows.pic: A verifier tosses r coins and reads q positions of a long proof string; the reader corrupts proof bits and watches the rejection probability respond.

rawFullRows.name: PCP theorem
rawFullRows.pic: A satisfiable formula’s PCP proof passes every random check, while for any proof of an unsatisfiable one a constant fraction of checks fail, as a histogram over coin tosses shows.

rawFullRows.name: PCP theorem is equivalent to hardness of approximating MAX-3SAT
rawFullRows.pic: Each random check of the verifier becomes a small set of clauses; the fraction of satisfiable clauses mirrors the acceptance probability, shown for honest and corrupted proofs.

rawFullRows.name: Fourier analysis of Boolean functions
rawFullRows.pic: A Boolean function on n bits is expanded in parity characters; its Fourier spectrum is drawn as bars, Parseval’s identity checks the total weight, and the reader edits the truth table.

rawFullRows.name: Blum–Luby–Rubinfeld linearity test
rawFullRows.pic: Test f(x) ⊕ f(y) = f(x ⊕ y) at random points; the rejection rate is plotted against the distance to the nearest linear function for functions the reader corrupts.

rawFullRows.name: Exponential-size PCPs from the Walsh–Hadamard code
rawFullRows.pic: An assignment is encoded by the Hadamard code of itself and of its tensor square; the verifier’s three tests — linearity, consistency, satisfaction — are stepped through with queries highlighted.

rawFullRows.name: Dinur’s gap amplification
rawFullRows.pic: A constraint graph is regularized, made an expander and powered; the unsatisfiable fraction (the gap) roughly doubles each round, plotted against round number.

rawFullRows.name: Parallel repetition theorem
rawFullRows.pic: A two-prover game is played k times in parallel; the best strategies’ winning probability is computed for small games and decays exponentially, though not simply as the k-th power.

rawFullRows.name: Håstad’s 3-bit PCP: 7/8 is optimal for MAX-3SAT
rawFullRows.pic: A random assignment satisfies 7/8 of clauses; a slider for any better ratio shows the reduction from Håstad’s verifier, which reads three bits and checks their parity, ruling it out unless P = NP.

rawFullRows.name: Hardness of approximating CLIQUE (FGLSS)
rawFullRows.pic: Nodes are accepting views of the verifier and edges join consistent views; large cliques correspond to good proofs, drawn for a toy verifier.

rawFullRows.name: Set cover cannot be approximated much better than ln n
rawFullRows.pic: The greedy algorithm’s ln n guarantee is plotted beside the hardness threshold from label cover, which nearly meets it.

rawFullRows.name: Goemans–Williamson MAX-CUT by semidefinite programming
rawFullRows.pic: Vertices become unit vectors on a sphere and a random hyperplane cuts them; the expected cut, at least 0.878 of the relaxation, is checked over many hyperplanes.

rawFullRows.name: Unique Games Conjecture
rawFullRows.pic: Label-cover instances whose constraints are permutations: a slider for the completeness and soundness gap, and a table of problems whose approximation thresholds the conjecture would settle, 0.878 for MAX-CUT among them.

rawFullRows.name: Proof Verification and Hardness of Approximation Problems

paper.authors: Sanjeev Arora, Carsten Lund, Rajeev Motwani, Madhu Sudan and Mario Szegedy
paper.title: Proof Verification and the Hardness of Approximation Problems

rawFullRows.pic: A verifier tosses coins and reads only a few bits of a long proof: the reader corrupts a fraction of a valid proof and watches the rejection rate, then sees the same gap reappear as a MAX-3SAT instance in which no assignment beats a fixed fraction of clauses.

rawFullRows.name: Decision trees and certificate complexity
rawFullRows.pic: Build a decision tree for OR or majority by choosing which bit to query next; its depth is compared with the certificate size the tool computes for each input.

rawFullRows.name: Sensitivity theorem (Huang)
rawFullRows.pic: For functions the reader edits on a small cube, sensitivity, block sensitivity and degree are computed; any large induced subgraph of the cube is shown to contain a vertex of degree at least √n.

rawFullRows.name: Yao’s minimax principle
rawFullRows.pic: A matrix of deterministic algorithms against inputs: the best randomized algorithm’s worst case equals the hardest input distribution’s best deterministic cost, computed by linear programming.

rawFullRows.name: Two-party communication complexity
rawFullRows.pic: Alice and Bob each hold n bits; a protocol tree partitions the input matrix into monochromatic rectangles, which are coloured as the reader steps through the protocol.

rawFullRows.name: Fooling sets and the rank bound: equality needs n bits
rawFullRows.pic: The identity matrix of EQUALITY has 2ⁿ diagonal cells, no two in one monochromatic rectangle; the matrix rank readout gives the same n-bit bound.

rawFullRows.name: Fingerprinting: equality with O(log n) random bits
rawFullRows.pic: Alice sends her string as a polynomial evaluated at a random point; differing strings collide with small probability, measured over many trials as n grows.

rawFullRows.name: Disjointness needs linear communication
rawFullRows.pic: The disjointness matrix has a large fooling set of complementary pairs; even randomized protocols the reader designs fail on the hard distribution unless they send many bits.

rawFullRows.name: Karchmer–Wigderson games
rawFullRows.pic: Alice holds a 1-input and Bob a 0-input of f; walking down a formula for f finds a differing coordinate, and the protocol’s length equals the formula’s depth.

rawFullRows.name: Håstad’s switching lemma
rawFullRows.pic: Randomly fix most variables of a DNF with small terms; the decision-tree depth of what remains is computed over many restrictions, and its histogram has an exponentially small tail.

rawFullRows.name: Parity is not in AC⁰
rawFullRows.pic: Restrictions collapse a constant-depth circuit layer by layer, yet parity of the surviving variables never simplifies; the required size is plotted against depth.

rawFullRows.name: Razborov–Smolensky: parity is not in AC⁰[3]
rawFullRows.pic: Each gate of a circuit with mod-3 gates is approximated by a low-degree polynomial over GF(3); the fraction of inputs where the approximation errs is tallied gate by gate.

rawFullRows.name: Williams: NEXP is not in ACC⁰
rawFullRows.pic: The proof strategy is drawn as a chain: a slightly faster-than-brute-force satisfiability algorithm for ACC⁰ circuits plus the nondeterministic time hierarchy yields the lower bound.

rawFullRows.name: Razborov: monotone circuits for CLIQUE are exponential
rawFullRows.pic: Monotone gates are approximated by sunflower-trimmed families of small cliques; the errors introduced on positive and negative test graphs are counted per gate.

rawFullRows.name: Ben-Or: algebraic decision trees for element distinctness
rawFullRows.pic: The yes-region of “all n numbers distinct” in ℝⁿ splits into n! connected cells; the reader probes points in three dimensions and the cell count lower-bounds the depth by n log n.

rawFullRows.name: Algebraic complexity: VP versus VNP
rawFullRows.pic: Arithmetic circuits for the determinant grow polynomially, while the best known for the permanent grow exponentially; both sizes are plotted against n.

rawFullRows.name: Natural proofs barrier (Razborov–Rudich)
rawFullRows.pic: A “natural” property that distinguishes hard functions from easy ones would also distinguish pseudorandom functions from random ones; the distinguisher is run and breaks the generator.

rawFullRows.name: Propositional proof systems (Cook–Reckhow)
rawFullRows.pic: A proof system is a fast checker for claimed tautology proofs; the reader submits proofs in different systems and watches the checker accept or reject each line.

rawFullRows.name: NP = coNP iff some proof system is polynomially bounded
rawFullRows.pic: A short proof for every tautology would be a coNP certificate and vice versa; both directions are drawn as arrows between a verifier and a proof system.

rawFullRows.name: Resolution
rawFullRows.pic: Resolve clauses on complementary literals by dragging them together; the derivation is drawn as a DAG ending in the empty clause for an unsatisfiable formula.

rawFullRows.name: DPLL and CDCL solvers produce resolution proofs
rawFullRows.pic: A backtracking SAT solver runs on a typed formula; each conflict learns a clause, and the run is converted into a resolution refutation whose size matches the solver’s work.

rawFullRows.name: Haken: pigeonhole formulas need exponential resolution proofs
rawFullRows.pic: The formula “n + 1 pigeons fit in n holes” is refuted by solvers for growing n; refutation sizes are plotted on a log scale against the exponential lower bound.

rawFullRows.name: Tseitin formulas on expanders are hard for resolution
rawFullRows.pic: Parity constraints on the edges of a graph with odd total charge are unsatisfiable; on a cycle the refutation is short, on an expander it explodes, both measured.

rawFullRows.name: Cutting planes prove pigeonhole efficiently
rawFullRows.pic: Pigeonhole clauses become linear inequalities; adding them up and rounding derives 0 ≥ 1 in a handful of lines that the reader can step through.

rawFullRows.name: The hierarchy of proof systems
rawFullRows.pic: Resolution, cutting planes, Frege and extended Frege are arranged by simulation arrows, with the formula families that separate them attached to each arrow.

rawFullRows.name: Exponential Time Hypothesis
rawFullRows.pic: Running times of the best known 3SAT algorithms are plotted as cⁿ with c falling over the decades toward but never reaching 1, the assumption being that some c > 1 is necessary.

rawFullRows.name: Schöning’s random-walk algorithm for k-SAT
rawFullRows.pic: Restart a short random walk from fresh random assignments; the number of restarts needed on random 3SAT instances grows like (4/3)ⁿ, beating the 2ⁿ of brute force.

rawFullRows.name: Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis
rawFullRows.pic: The base of the best k-SAT algorithm is plotted against k and approaches 2; the hypothesis says it really does tend to 2.

rawFullRows.name: Orthogonal vectors are hard under SETH
rawFullRows.pic: Split the variables of a CNF in half and list all partial assignments as vectors; a satisfying assignment appears as an orthogonal pair, found by the reader’s search.

rawFullRows.name: No strongly subquadratic edit distance under SETH
rawFullRows.pic: The quadratic dynamic-programming table for edit distance fills on two typed strings; gadget strings encoding orthogonal-vectors instances show why skipping most of it would refute SETH.

rawFullRows.name: 3SUM conjecture
rawFullRows.pic: The quadratic two-pointer algorithm finds three numbers summing to zero in a sorted list; its step count is plotted against n², the conjectured barrier.

rawFullRows.name: All-pairs shortest paths conjecture
rawFullRows.pic: The cubic Floyd–Warshall table fills for a weighted graph; problems shown equivalent to it under subcubic reductions, such as negative-triangle detection, are listed beside it.

rawFullRows.name: Fixed-parameter tractability: vertex cover by bounded search
rawFullRows.pic: Branch on the two endpoints of any uncovered edge; the search tree has depth k and at most 2ᵏ leaves, so large graphs with small covers are solved quickly, timed live.

rawFullRows.name: Kernelization
rawFullRows.pic: Reduction rules for vertex cover — take high-degree vertices, drop isolated ones — shrink a large graph to a kernel with at most k² edges before any search begins.

rawFullRows.name: CLIQUE is W[1]-hard
rawFullRows.pic: Running times for k-clique by brute force grow like n^k while vertex cover grows like 2ᵏ·n; the two families of curves are plotted to show which parameter can be tamed.

rawFullRows.name: Distributional problems and average-case tractability
rawFullRows.pic: Run a SAT solver on random 3SAT instances at different clause densities; running time peaks near the satisfiability threshold and is easy on either side.

rawFullRows.name: Levin: complete problems for distributional NP
rawFullRows.pic: Bounded tiling under a simple distribution is hard on average if any distributional NP problem is; the reduction compresses probable instances into short tiling seeds.

rawFullRows.name: Samplable distributions
rawFullRows.pic: A sampler program generates instances; the reader compares its output histogram with the target distribution and with an unsamplable one defined by Kolmogorov complexity.

rawFullRows.name: BQP
rawFullRows.pic: A small quantum circuit acts on a state vector of 2ⁿ amplitudes; measurement probabilities are computed exactly, and the acceptance probability must clear 2/3 or fall below 1/3.

rawFullRows.name: BPP ⊆ BQP ⊆ PSPACE
rawFullRows.pic: Final amplitudes are computed as sums over all computational paths, one path at a time, with memory that stays polynomial; the running time doubles with each added gate.

rawFullRows.name: Quantum search lower bound (Bennett–Bernstein–Brassard–Vazirani)
rawFullRows.pic: The amplitude on the marked item can grow only a little per query; the bound is plotted against the number of queries and Grover’s √N schedule touches it.

rawFullRows.name: A Theory of the Learnable
rawFullRows.pic: A hidden conjunction of literals labels random examples from a distribution the reader shapes; Valiant’s elimination algorithm learns a hypothesis, and its true error falls below ε with probability at least 1 − δ once the sample passes (n ln 3 + ln 1/δ)/ε.
